title: 1844 in Cadiz
source: Chronicling America, LCCN sn84028793. Names as printed. No invented people.

entities.name: Miss Sarah Ritchey
entities.place: Steubenville street, front room, second story of Joseph R. Hunter's dwelling house, opposite John Beall's Drug Store
entities.note: Milliner and mantua making. Card dated Cadiz, March 8, 1844. The card falls out of later numbers; do not pretend she is still there in September.

entities.name: DAY LIGHT AND FAIR PLAY
entities.place: Cadiz Hotel livery, formerly Levi Mallernee. J. S. / Wm. N. Maffit, agent
entities.note: Hack to St. Clairsville, Wednesdays and Saturdays. Standing card dated Cadiz, Nov. 16th, 1843. No railroad in this run.

entities.name: Thomas Hogg public auction
entities.place: Cadiz. He is leaving the country
entities.note: Wagon, stock, furniture, pasture lots. First Monday of April. Dissolution from J. P. Wood is in the same March 21 paper.

entities.name: John Selby farm
entities.place: Cadiz township, joining George Day and John Hines
entities.note: Land for sale in the March 21 paper. Not a shop on the square.

entities.name: Doct. L. Voorhies
entities.place: With Dr. J. Pearce
entities.note: Card from 21 March. He marries Margaret Lafferty, all of this place, Wednesday morning 1 May (2 May paper, type only).

entities.name: Edward T. Huebener
entities.place: Bedwell and Huebener stone-cutting shop
entities.note: Leaving in the spring. Card from 28 March.

entities.name: Western Exchange
entities.place: Cadiz. Stand formerly Thos. D. Grimes. A. P. Croskey [later cards also A. F.]
entities.note: First card 28 March. Volunteers later told to meet at the Exchange Saturday 25 May. Do not mix with R. H. Legget's Western Exchange Hotel in Carrollton.

entities.name: Western Exchange Hotel, Carrollton
entities.place: Carrollton. Stage office. R. H. Legget
entities.note: Not Cadiz. Printed 18 April as a through-card.

entities.name: Stanton and Peppard
entities.place: Opposite James McNutt's Hotel
entities.note: E. M. Stanton, S. G. Peppard. Card from 28 March.

entities.name: Cummins and Harper
entities.place: Steubenville street, opposite the public buildings. For a time, inside the Sentinel office
entities.note: Lecky Harper. 'Our Law Office is at present in the office of the Sentinel,' 4 April.

entities.name: S. W. Bostwick
entities.place: Cadiz attorney
entities.note: Standing card from 21 March.

entities.name: T. L. Jewett
entities.place: Cadiz attorney
entities.note: Standing card from 21 March.

entities.name: M. H. Urquhart
entities.place: Cadiz attorney
entities.note: Standing card from 21 March.

entities.name: L. P. Milligan
entities.place: Cadiz. Crabb and Roberts later sit in his frame building on Market street, opposite Kilgore & Co.
entities.note: Standing attorney card from 21 March.

entities.name: William Sharp, tin shop
entities.place: Cadiz. Standing Market Street tin / copper card
entities.note: 4 April: twelve cents reward, but no charges, for John Milligan, indented apprentice, ran 2 April. The boy is not found again in this run.

entities.name: McNutt and Smith, ploughs
entities.place: Cadiz. Address only from 21 March
entities.note: Standing plough card.

entities.name: John Beall, drugs
entities.place: Steubenville street / public-buildings neighborhood. Ritchey is opposite
entities.note: Also P. M. on the April 1 and July 1 letter lists. Sands's sarsaparilla; Jew David's plaster agent.

entities.name: Washingtonian House
entities.place: Uhrichsville. M. B. Haskins
entities.note: Temperance / cold-water house. Not on the Cadiz square.

entities.name: A. S. Canfield, Variety Store
entities.place: One door west of Thomas Hogg's old stand, room formerly George Craig
entities.note: Dry goods, queensware, glassware, hardware, groceries, iron, nails, glass and domestic goods. Cash or approved country produce. First card 18 April.

entities.name: Rea & Eaton
entities.place: Opposite the Jail Buildings, immediately under the Sentinel office
entities.note: John Rea and David Eaton purchased the boot and shoe establishment of Mr. John Phillips. The paper is upstairs. The boots are downstairs. First card 18 April.

entities.name: Snyder & Mallernee
entities.place: Old stand of Snyder & Moore
entities.note: Samuel Snyder, Emanuel Mallernee, tailoring. First card 18 April.

entities.name: Crabb and Roberts
entities.place: Milligan frame, Market street, opposite Kilgore and Co.
entities.note: Tailors. First card 4 April.

entities.name: Samuel Timmons
entities.place: Corner brick opposite Hogg's old stand
entities.note: Saddle, harness, trunk. First card 4 April.

entities.name: J. W. Beebe and Co.
entities.place: Cheap store opposite the treasurer's office
entities.note: First card 11 April. 6000 yds. brown and bleached muslins (fabric, not a surname). W. B. Beebe later Cadiz agent for Wistar's balsam.

clips.headline: NEW SPRING GOODS AT THE CHEAP STORE

entities.name: Stewart, Milligan and Bennett
entities.place: The Bennett stand
entities.note: James Stewart, William Milligan, R. J. Bennett. New at the Bennett stand 4 April. William Bennett sells his entire property and merchandize to them 18 April.

entities.name: J. M'Gonagle valedictory
entities.place: The Sentinel office
entities.note: 21 March 1844. He sells to L. Harper. Next Thursday the masthead reads Edited by L. Harper.

entities.name: L. Harper in the chair
entities.place: The Sentinel office
entities.note: First number 28 March. From 22 May he prints every Wednesday. Campaign paper $1.50 in advance.

entities.name: Trading Wives
entities.place: A few miles of this place
entities.note: Local item in the 21 March paper. Not a shop card.

entities.name: Texas as it arrived
entities.place: Set in type at Cadiz when the exchanges sent it
entities.note: April numbers fill with Texas. 25 April: Madisonian, treaty of annexation signed; the office does not expect action this session. The walk already spends Turner & Divine in September. Do not spend that joke here.

entities.name: Married / Died
entities.place: Local vitals as printed that week
entities.note: Names as the office set them. No surname hunt.

entities.name: Dickinson and Co.
entities.place: Forwarding, Cumberland, Md.
entities.note: A through-card, not a Cadiz depot.

threads.title: The chair changes
threads.body: Thursday, 21 March 1844, J. M'Gonagle prints his valedictory and sells the Sentinel to L. Harper. The next Thursday the masthead reads Edited by L. Harper. From 22 May he prints every Wednesday. That is the press talking about itself. The paper upstairs does not move. The boots downstairs arrive later.

threads.title: The square fills in
threads.body: Each Thursday a new door takes a stand. Hogg is leaving the country. Ritchey is upstairs on Steubenville street, opposite Beall's drugs. Croskey takes the Exchange, formerly Grimes. Stanton and Peppard sit opposite McNutt's. Rea and Eaton buy Phillips's shoe shop, immediately under the Sentinel, opposite the jail. The paper is upstairs. The boots are downstairs.

stops.label: Canfield, one door west of Hogg

threads.title: The only timetable
threads.body: No railroad is printed in this run. The town's timetable is a standing card: DAY LIGHT AND FAIR PLAY. J. S. and Wm. N. Maffit bought the livery formerly Levi Mallernee. The hack to St. Clairsville leaves Wednesdays and Saturdays. Wednesday becomes print day from 22 May. The hack also leaves on Wednesday.

threads.title: Texas as it arrived
threads.body: The office sets Texas when the exchanges send it. It is not a Cadiz argument until the office makes it one. April 11 the heading is TEXAS. April 25 the Madisonian: the treaty of annexation is signed; the office does not expect action this session. By June the paper comes over to Polk and Dallas. That later type is on the shelf, not recorded yet.

stops.label: Treaty signed, no action this session

later.label: Voorhies marries Margaret Lafferty. Democratic meeting at McNutt's.
Spring Term. Ohio vs. Eady — that case is Ady. Murray of Deersville murdered.
Four weeklies in one town. Gould stabbing of McConnell. Texas treaty printed. Editor absent.
Hickory Club, Saturday next, early candle-lighting, house of Jas. McNutt.
Paper comes over to Polk and Dallas. Ads crowded out.
Fourth of July in Sharp's oak grove. Hickory pole vs poplar stick.
THE LIST in the shop windows. Planned destruction of the Sentinel office. Gimblet hill.
ATTEMPT TO ASSASSINATE THE EDITOR. ANNEXATION. hung over a local marriage.
Freeport report. Hero of the skillet. A GLANCE AT TEXAS leads the paper.
